evidence.summary: The TypeScript client can start a thread, continue it with another run, or reconstruct a prior thread from its ID.
Integrations can label a thread at creation with threadSource. A resumed thread retains the original source.
Structured config is applied before raw configOverrides. Managed SDK settings follow. These overrides leave configuration files unchanged.
The SDK is described for coding automation and CI. The app server is the documented surface for custom clients handling authentication, conversation history, approvals and streamed agent events.
startThread constructs one Thread object. resumeThread constructs a Thread with the supplied ID.
A new Thread starts with an unset ID and stores the ID from thread.started. runStreamed exposes events, while run collects items and final response.
The CLI arguments contain a thread source only when a source is set and there is no existing thread ID.
The wrapper appends structured configuration, then raw overrides, then managed options such as the base URL and model.
Structured inputs can include local image paths. Input normalization separates those paths from text.
The repository README distinguishes buffered run from incremental structured events via runStreamed.
The open Issue asks about creating, running and resuming multiple sessions through the TypeScript SDK. It gives no acceptance criteria for a dedicated orchestration API.
The open Issue requests an official Java SDK or a supported Java App Server client. Suggested scope includes account login and thread/turn lifecycle.

cases.question: How much of the multi-session request can be established from the documented TypeScript interfaces?

claims.text: Individual threads can be created and resumed.
A built-in multi-session orchestration API is established by the cited material.
The issue is a request/question rather than a release record.

cases.question: Can the Java integration feature be promoted to a supported product rule based on this issue?

claims.text: An official Java SDK or supported Java client was requested.
The requested Java SDK is already released.
The app server is a documented integration surface for custom clients.

cases.question: Can resuming an existing thread overwrite its origin label via threadSource?

claims.text: The option is forwarded for creation without an existing thread ID.
Resuming preserves the existing origin label.
Supplying a new source label during resume replaces the old label.

cases.question: What is the order of per-client configuration overrides?

claims.text: Structured configuration precedes raw overrides.
Managed SDK options are appended later.
These SDK overrides rewrite Codex configuration files.

cases.question: Which SDK call allows a caller to handle incremental turn events?

claims.text: runStreamed exposes an asynchronous event iterator.
run returns the collected turn result.
run has the same streaming return type as runStreamed.

cases.question: Is a fresh thread guaranteed to expose a reusable ID before its first turn?

claims.text: A fresh thread can have a null ID.
The SDK assigns the ID after the thread-started event.
startThread always allocates the final ID synchronously.

cases.question: Does the input schema support attaching local images with text?

claims.text: A structured local_image entry carries a local path.
The wrapper separates image paths from text.
The same input type guarantees remote image URLs are fetched automatically.

cases.question: Which surface does the official SDK page identify for clients that own login, history and approvals?

claims.text: The page points custom clients to the app server.
The SDK supports coding automation and programmatic local threads.
The cited SDK thread methods establish the full custom-client protocol.
